newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Most LatAm stocks seen firmer this week on rebound.
newsitem.headline: Most LatAm stocks seen firmer this week on rebound.

text.p: Stocks on most Latin American bolsas were seen rising moderately this week, rebounding some from steep falls on Friday sparked by comments by U.S. Fed Chairman Alan Greenspan that roiled both U.S. and overseas markets, analysts said.

Greenspan wondered in a speech Thursday evening how to measure whether "irrational exuberance has unduly escalated asset values..." His remarks were widely interpreted as heralding a correction in stock prices and tighter Fed policy.
But on Monday, stock trade in the U.S. and abroad was recovering and the impact of the comments had died down.
Brazilian shares were likely to be boosted by news on the telecommunications front, including the presentation to Congress of a bill containing a new general telecom law.
Brokers said increases would be tempered by volatility ahead of next Monday's options settlements.
The Bovespa index of the 49 most traded stocks climbed 3.1 percent last week to 68,729 points in strong turnover.
In Argentina, stocks were seen consolidating after sharp gains last week, when the MerVal Index rose 1.57 percent to 626,63 points despite falling Friday.
"The market will only consolidate its higher trend," said Hugo Diaz Lourenco, chief analyst at Consultants CE.
Lourenco added that investors may continue buying more selectively to pick stocks that so far have not benefitted from the generally upbeat mood.
Chilean shares are likely to to regain some ground after taking a drubbing last week, when the blue-chip IPSA dropped 3.33 percent to 89.55 points, its lowest level this year.
But no big gains are expected.
"It won't get beaten up again like last week, but I think the bolsa will stay more or less flat," said Ida Longeri, research director at brokers Larrain Vial.
Bargain-hunters will probably move back in and movements on the fixed-income market suggest investors are betting on an early relaxation of interest rates, possibly as early as January, she added.
In Venezuela, despite some bounce-back from Friday's Greenspan-related slump, stocks were seen mostly flat this week in thin trade as investors wind down ahead of the Christmas holiday, traders said.
Brokers do not expect much activity this week despite the high-profile privatizations of Venezuelan banks Banco de Venezuela and Banco Consolidado, which are set for December 19.
The bolsa's 19-share index finished a lackluster week down 1.5 percent at 6,097.42 points.
